newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Wells Rich optmistic over GGT deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Wells Rich optmistic over GGT deal.

text.p: Wells Rich Greene BDDP chairman Frank Assumma said the proposed takeover of his agency by Britain's GGT would be the "best possible outcome" among a range of options explored in recent months.

"We really felt it was absolutely the best alternative for our clients and employees and, in the long run, for shareholders as well," said Assumma in an interview with Reuters, "It's a good strategic fit that will work well for us and for our clients."
Wells Rich is the U.S. unit of Paris-based BDDP, which has been on the auction block for months.
Wells Rich was previously examined by WPP Plc, Cordiant Plc nd Grey Advertising, among others, according to industy sources.
BDDP and Wells Rich had also explored a leveraged buyout of the agency.
The New York agency also battled rumors that it would be closed and its accounts parceled out to competitors under some scenarios being considered.

But Assumma said that the takeover proposal has full backing of BDDP management internationally and lifts the cloud that had been hovering over Wells Rich, the 20th largest U.S. agency with annual billings of $850 million.

Wells Rich's major clients, including Procter & Gamble, Liberty Mutual, Heineken USA, Bristol-Myers Squibb and Hertz, were informed of the deal. Assumma said "they were all quite happy with it since it meant there would be continuity in our business."
Assumma also said that the deal would enhance prospects for international business, which is increasingly important in servicing global consumer products clients.

A number of the deals being considered were rejected because the proposed acquirer represented companies that competed with Wells Rich's clients. But the GGT merger would not pose any significant conflicts, Assumma said.
BDDP, while giving a long look to a proposed leveraged buyout as an alternative to an outside takeover, concluded that "it would have been much too difficult from a debt standpoint," Assumma said.
In the end, GGT's proposal was the most attractive and Assumma said that while the deal is not final "This is a bid completely supported by the management of BDDP on a worldwide basis."
